U.S. Forest Service Releases More Bigfoot Sightings
Hair-Covered Creatures Known as "Sasquatch" and "Bigfoot"
More Than 16,000 Reports Registered with the Bigfoot Mapping Project

The U.S. Forest Service has released new accounts from people who say they have seen Bigfoot, the legendary creature.


A scene from the film "Sasquatch Sunset." Courtesy of Studio DHL.

View original image

On November 22, the British newspaper The Guardian reported that the U.S. Forest Service had recently released reports on sightings of Bigfoot in Montana and Oregon, as well as evidence related to the sightings.

In forested areas of the northwestern United States, people sometimes report seeing a hairy creature known as Sasquatch. It is said to walk upright like a human and live hidden in deep forests. The nickname Bigfoot comes from the huge footprints it is said to leave in the woods.

The newly released report details how wildlife biologist Rodney Johnson investigated strange, unidentified footprints at three sites in the Umatilla National Forest in northeastern Oregon in 1982. After examining them, he concluded they were unlikely to belong to a Sasquatch, citing eight reasons, including that the stride length did not change even on slopes and that the footprints were not deeply embedded in the mud at two sites.

In a follow-up report, Forest Service investigators wrote that "the tracks were an obvious attempt to perpetrate a hoax" and that "we believe this memo should be sufficient to close the Bigfoot case."

Additional materials released by the Forest Service included an account from Montana resident Leo Kinney, who said that in the 1980s he went into the woods to look for an elk carcass and "found another kind of creature that walked on its hind legs." Although he did not see the creature itself, he said he found footprints, detected a strong odor, and heard a growling sound. He added that he believed the creature had dragged the elk away and chose not to follow it.

The materials also included a 2003 article in a local Montana newspaper about Bigfoot footprints and an account from someone who claimed to have seen a bear-like creature near a creek in Montana.

In June this year, a report also came in from a rural town in Ontario, eastern Canada, where someone said they had seen a large figure matching Bigfoot's characteristics. Residents said they had seen two creatures rummaging through a pile of garbage, describing them as "one large and one small, with the smaller one cinnamon-colored."

Meanwhile, more than 16,000 Bigfoot-related reports have reportedly been registered with the Bigfoot Mapping Project, which collects records of animals and creatures whose existence has not been proven.


Josh Redstone, a professor of philosophy at Carleton University in the United States, said, "Bigfoot is a prime example of how much curiosity an unproven existence can inspire in people."
